title: Berlin Evaluation of Aortic sTenosis and timing
summary:
Aortic valve stenosis (AS) remains frequently underdiagnosed and undertreated despite its high clinical relevance. Many patients experience substantial delays between the onset of initial symptoms and the performance of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), while a considerable proportion of older individuals living in the general population remain unaware of their disease.

The present project aims to systematically quantify both the pre-procedural care pathway and the burden of previously undetected asymptomatic AS in Berlin. This will generate robust, locally relevant data that can serve as a foundation for optimizing diagnostic and therapeutic pathways, targeted medical education, patient awareness initiatives, and population-based screening strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cohort 1:
Minimum age of 18 years
Ability to provide informed consent
Planned transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)
Severe aortic valve stenosis
No valve-in-valve procedures

Cohort 2:
Age >70 years
Asymptomatic
Residence in Berlin
Ability to provide informed consent
No previously diagnosed aortic valve stenosis
Exclusion criteria:
Cohort 1:
Age <18 years
Unable to provide informed consent
Valve-in-valve procedures


Cohort 2:
Age <70 years
Presence of cardiac symptoms
Residence outside Berlin
Unable to provide informed consent
Previously diagnosed aortic valve stenosis
